title: Wheels Not Rotating
shortDescription: Polaris 360/280 pressure-side cleaner's wheels aren't turning despite water flow.
fullDescription:
When the Polaris 360 or 280 cleaner's wheels don't rotate, the drive belt or gearbox is usually at fault. Debris can jam the drive shaft, or the belts can stretch or break over time.

This is the #1 service issue on pressure-side cleaners. Most owners can replace belts in under 30 minutes with a small screwdriver and a belt loop tool.
symptoms: Cleaner drifts but wheels don't turn

fixSteps.title: Inspect belts
fixSteps.instruction: Flip cleaner over, remove wheel covers, inspect all three belts for cracks or stretching.

fixSteps.title: Replace belts
fixSteps.instruction: Install Polaris belt kit 6-605-00; align belt with gear teeth.

whenToCallPro: If belt replacement doesn't restore motion, the gearbox needs a pool tech.
videoSearchQuery: Polaris 360 belt replacement wheels not turning

faq.a: Every 1-2 years in typical residential use.

title: Hose Tangling or Twisting
shortDescription: Feed hose twists itself or gets stuck, preventing full pool coverage.
fullDescription:
Polaris pressure-side cleaners rely on a spring-loaded swivel on the feed hose. When the swivel seizes, the hose starts twisting as the cleaner turns, eventually parking itself in one spot.

UV damage and heavy use wear out the UWF (universal wall fitting) swivels. Replacement is straightforward.
symptoms: Cleaner parks and spins in place

fixSteps.title: Check swivels
fixSteps.instruction: Each hose section has a swivel; rotate by hand — should spin freely.

fixSteps.title: Replace UWF
fixSteps.instruction: Unscrew seized swivel and install new UWF D20 at the wall fitting.

faq.a: Reach the farthest point of pool plus 6-12 inches, no more.

title: Backup Valve Not Cycling
shortDescription: Cleaner gets stuck in corners because the backup valve fails to fire.
fullDescription:
The backup valve (Polaris 6-504-00) diverts water flow every 3-5 minutes to reverse the cleaner out of corners. When its internal mechanism wears out, the cleaner parks in corners and stops cleaning effectively.

Replacement is direct — the valve plugs into the feed hose with hose clamps.
symptoms: Cleaner stuck in corner for 10+ minutes

fixSteps.title: Observe valve cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Watch cleaner for 5 minutes — expect 2-3 backup pulses.

fixSteps.title: Replace valve
fixSteps.instruction: Install Polaris 6-504-00 backup valve inline in feed hose.

whenToCallPro: Booster pump pressure issues require a tech.

title: Alpha iQ Motor Overload
shortDescription: Polaris Alpha iQ robotic cleaner motor has detected an overload.
fullDescription:
Error 01 on Polaris Alpha iQ and other robotic cleaners indicates a motor overload. The drive or pump motor drew excessive current and the controller shut it down.

Tangled debris around tracks, a stuck impeller, or a seized bearing typically cause this. Checking tracks and impeller usually resolves it.

causes.cause: Debris stuck in tracks or impeller

fixSteps.title: Inspect impeller
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cover and clear debris from impeller.

fixSteps.title: Clean tracks
fixSteps.instruction: Remove hair and debris from drive tracks and sprockets.

videoSearchQuery: Polaris Alpha iQ Err 01 motor overload

faq.a: Clear debris first — repeated overloads can burn the motor.

title: Alpha iQ Power Supply Fault
shortDescription: Robotic cleaner power supply detected a voltage fault.
fullDescription:
Error 02 means the low-voltage power supply or cable has a fault. Most often caused by a nicked floating cable or water intrusion in the connector at the cleaner body.

Inspect the full cable length for cuts and check the connector O-ring.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cable
fixSteps.instruction: Walk cable length, look for abrasion or cuts.

videoSearchQuery: Polaris Alpha iQ Err 02 power supply

faq.q: Can I repair a nicked cable?
faq.a: No — waterproof integrity is critical; replace the entire cable.

title: Weak Cleaning Suction
shortDescription: Cleaner picks up water but barely grabs debris.
fullDescription:
On pressure-side cleaners, weak cleaning usually traces to booster pump or jet issues. On robotic cleaners, a full debris canister or clogged filter is almost always the cause.

Clean the filter after every cycle for best performance.
symptoms: Cleaner moves but doesn't pick up

fixSteps.title: Empty bag/canister
fixSteps.instruction: Open debris chamber and rinse filter screens.

whenToCallPro: Booster pump issues require a tech.

faq.a: Every cycle for robotic; weekly for pressure-side bag.

title: Cleaner Won't Climb Walls
shortDescription: Robotic cleaner stays on floor, won't climb walls or waterline.
fullDescription:
If an Alpha iQ, 9550 Sport, or similar robot stops climbing, the drive tracks are worn, impeller fouled, or the cycle program is set to floor-only.

Check the app/controller for cycle mode first — many users accidentally set floor mode.

causes.cause: Cycle mode set to floor only

fixSteps.title: Check cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Set cleaner to 'Floor, Walls, Waterline' cycle in app.

fixSteps.title: Inspect tracks
fixSteps.instruction: Look for glazed rubber on tracks — replace if smooth.

videoSearchQuery: Polaris Alpha iQ won't climb walls

faq.a: Yes — very slick tiles may prevent climbing; check Polaris compatibility.

title: Out of Water Detected
shortDescription: Alpha iQ robot's water sensor indicates it is not fully submerged.
fullDescription:
Error 05 appears when the cleaner is powered on out of water or when the water sensor fails. This prevents the motor from running dry.

If the cleaner is in water and still shows Err 05, the sensor may be dirty or failed.

fixSteps.title: Fully submerge
fixSteps.instruction: Let cleaner sink to bottom for 30 seconds before starting cycle.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe water sensor (small probe on housing) with a soft cloth.

videoSearchQuery: Polaris Alpha iQ Err 05 out of water

faq.a: No — running dry burns the motor in minutes.
